sources.publisher: Presidency of the Republic of Moldova
sources.title: Official biography: education, public service and presidential terms
sources.findings: Read the official presidential biography for birthday May 24, 1972 in Risipeni, 1994 management graduation, 1995–1998 international-relations studies, 2010–2012 World Bank adviser role, education ministry July 2012–July 2015, party founding and resignation, 2019 premiership and both December 24 presidential accessions. Its Harvard public-policy degree wording conflicts with Harvard’s own MC/MPA record; use Harvard. Adviser to an executive director is not the executive director or World Bank president. No assumption that party founder remains party chair.

sources.title: Maia Sandu MC/MPA 2010: graduation-address announcement, 29 March 2022
sources.findings: Read Harvard Gazette’s March 29, 2022 announcement, including degree designation and prior studies/career. The awarded degree is the Mid-Career Master in Public Administration, MC/MPA 2010, not MPP. Mid-career describes the program, not proof she studied part-time while employed. The announcement’s shorthand about a December election is superseded by the presidential record’s November 15 vote and December 24 inauguration. A scheduled graduation speech is not proof it occurred; promotional praise is not independent measurement of corruption reduction.

sources.title: PAS founding congress and Justice Ministry registration, May 2016
sources.findings: Read MOLDPRES’s May 26, 2016 registration report. Distinguish the December 23, 2015 political-movement announcement, May 15 founding congress, May 19 submission and May 26 Justice Ministry registration. Contemporary party membership counts and then-current appointments are not carried into 2026 as current. The original article date is separate from the site’s moving current-date header.

sources.title: Sandu government loses no-confidence vote, 12 November 2019
sources.findings: Read Xinhua’s November 12, 2019 no-confidence account: 63 of 101 deputies supported dismissal, and the cabinet had taken office June 8. The dispute concerned Sandu’s proposed role in preselecting prosecutor-general candidates, not a criminal conviction of her or a sole unilateral final appointment. ACUM–Socialist coalition and head-of-government status are distinct from the presidency held by Dodon.

sources.title: Chicu government takes office on 14 November 2019
sources.findings: Read Xinhua’s completed successor-government swearing-in account. Dateline/event November 14, 2019 differs from November 15 page timestamp; Chicu’s cabinet received confidence and took the oath on November 14 after Sandu’s November 12 no-confidence vote. The article’s forecasts about government lifespan and reform promises are not adopted as fulfilled outcomes.

sources.title: Moldova country page: candidate status and accession process
sources.findings: Read the European Commission country page’s current candidate-country label and relevant accession chronology/search-indexed material. The latest-news entries concern an ongoing process, not completed membership. No exhaustive chapter-by-chapter or full 2026 Commission country-report audit claimed.

sources.publisher: Council of the European Union / European Council
sources.title: Moldova: candidacy, accession negotiations and 2026 developments
sources.findings: Read the Council/European Council policy page’s accession sections. March 3, 2022 application, June 23 candidate decision, December 2023 political opening decision, June 21, 2024 negotiating framework and June 25 conference are distinct. The page also records October 13, 2026 opening of clusters 2 and 3. Public text acknowledges ongoing progress without claiming all negotiations closed, a fixed accession date or sole personal responsibility.

sources.title: First Accession Conference with Moldova, 25 June 2024
sources.findings: Read the first accession-conference page. It identifies the June 25, 2024 meeting and Moldova’s delegation led by Prime Minister Dorin Recean. Sandu’s policy advocacy is not a personal signature of an accession treaty or personal chairing of that delegation. Candidate and member status remain distinct.

sources.publisher: Constitutional Court of the Republic of Moldova
sources.title: Confirmation of the November 2024 presidential election and Sandu mandate
sources.findings: Read selected substantive sections of the Constitutional Court’s 2024 election-validation account: two rounds October 20 and November 3, CEC November 9 result, 930,139 votes for Sandu versus 750,430 for Stoianoglo, and validation requirements. The court confirmed the result while discussing vote-buying and electoral problems; validation is not a claim that no irregularity existed. Court records non-party status before validation, distinct from PAS support. No full underlying case file or individual vote-buying prosecution reviewed.

sources.title: Sandu sworn in for second presidential term, 24 December 2024
sources.findings: Read Interfax’s December 24, 2024 completed swearing-in report and final 55.35% runoff result. It independently corroborates the official biography’s second-term inauguration and 2020 victory over Dodon. The November 3 runoff is not October 20’s first round; no direct quotation of the oath or ceremonial speech reproduced. This historic event is not evidence of current personal activity.

sources.publisher: OSCE Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights
sources.title: 2024 presidential election and referendum: official summary of final findings
sources.findings: Read ODIHR’s official March 24, 2025 summary of final findings and recommendations on the 2024 presidential election and referendum. Preserve both positive administration/free-campaign findings and unequal-opportunity criticism involving favourable incumbent coverage and overlapping campaigns. This is a summary page, not a claimed full final-report PDF review. Do not convert observation findings into a criminal conviction or annulment of the election.

sources.title: November 2026 completed Brussels meeting with António Costa and enlargement remarks
sources.findings: Read MOLDPRES’s substantive completed Brussels meeting and enlargement-forum report, quoting Costa after meeting Sandu and describing her remarks. Search metadata dates publication November 16 at 19:05; the rendered global date header moves to November 18 and relative-age text varies. The official Costa schedule independently places the meeting on November 16, but the schedule alone is not proof of attendance. Combined with the retrospective report it supports the date. Early-2028 negotiation closure is Sandu’s goal, not completed membership; anticipated opening of remaining clusters is not recorded as already done.
